identity: A Modern Standard Arabic popular-science / technology magazine article headed الورق الإلكتروني الذكي (Smart Electronic Paper). Structure: a 3-token title line, then five body paragraphs delimited by <NL> at indices 3, 49, 147, 181, 353. Content arc: (P1) the predicted paperless office never arrived, paper use keeps rising; (P2) why paper still wins, and the coming 'smart paper'; (P3) wireless delivery to thin flexible readers; (P4) how electronic paper is physically built — charged bicolour plastic microspheres in a transparent flexible sheet, rollable cylinder displays; (P5) plastic transistors, electronic ink of titanium-dioxide flakes suspended in clear oil, signage use, and a one-line peroration. Register is expository / encyclopedic third-person science journalism — my doctrine's §B/§L. It is emphatically NOT narrative (§E), NOT hadith (§D), NOT first-person memoir (§H), and contains no dialogue, no page furniture, no Latin script, no URLs, no abbreviation dots. So none of §A, §D, §G, §H, §J apply here.
law: LAW 6 first: I read the register off the opening 200 tokens and set the §B/§L target of 12–20 tokens per sentence. The sentence unit here is the ASSERTION: one topic plus one predication, with every subordinate limb (relative الذي/التي, result بحيث, purpose/negative دون أن, temporal كلما, comparative مثل, and the جواب of a شرط) staying inside its main clause per LAW 4. The engine of segmentation in this text is LAW 1: this author builds paragraphs by chaining و + a fresh topic — والواضح، والسبب، والمؤكد، والورق الإلكتروني، وهكذا، ويمكنها، ولا يتعدى، وتنقسم، وعلى كل نصف، ومن مجموعها، وهناك، وسوف، وأثناء، ويمكن، ويتم، ويتميز، ومن ثم. Every one of those introduces a NEW argument (new subject, new topic NP, or a fronted PP with its own predication) and therefore takes a boundary before it. The counterweight is the phrase-level و, which I never cut: noun coordination (وخبراء، والمعرفة، والرسوم، وصحف ومجلات، والأخبار، وإعادة الكتابة)، adjective coordination (ومرنة، وخفيفة الوزن، والأسود)، participial coordination (والمدمجة، والتي تتميز)، bare VP chaining that shares the subject and adds no argument (ولم يقل أبدا، وتحدثها باستمرار)، paired attributes of one referent (قطرها ... وطولها)، and an elliptical alternative adjunct with no verb (وربما بشكل مباشر). Beyond LAW 1: ف opens a sentence when it is resumptive (فإذا ... twice, LAW 2 + C1) but never when it is the جواب الشرط or the ف of أما...فـ; إذ opens a segment (C3 / B2) even trailing, unlike لأن; أما...فـ is the hardest boundary in Arabic expository prose; a rhetorical question mark is a boundary (LAW 0 corollary); and لكن / حقا + إن open sentences. Result: 33 segments over 455 word tokens, mean 13.8 — squarely in the §B/§L band and well clear of my batch-1 habit of ~25.
reasoning: SITE 4–31 (28 tokens, kept whole). My longest segment and my first temptation to obey LAW 0 blindly. But منذ قدوم العصر الرقمي is a fronted temporal adjunct that attaches FORWARD (LAW 4 mirror case, the على ما يبدو precedent), and everything from أخذ العلماء onward hangs off the single predicate أخذ ... في إطلاق الوعود: بأننا is a complementizer, التي لا تستخدم a relative, and بل أجهزة إلكترونية a phrase-level correction of ورقا with no new predicate. There is no site inside it with a new argument, so no cut. Boundary at 31 (فقط) before لكن: this is a full-strength contrastive head of 17 tokens, not the short ولكن tail of B4, so it opens rather than trails. hi. || SITES 38 and 78 (إذ), my two med calls. Doctrine pulls both ways: LAW 4 says a trailing subordinate belongs to its main clause and lists لأن as a non-cutter, but C3 records إذ cutting twice in §C (@298, @619) and B2 lists it for §B, where its close cousin حيث is a confirmed cutter (doc_47764cf032d7 @762, and K2). I resolve for cutting: إذ is not a plain causal like لأن but a resumptive evidential move, and in both places here it launches an independent assertion (at 39 that paper use never fell; at 79 a thirty-percent statistic). Both clauses are substantial (10 and 22 tokens), which is comma-or-period territory, not the tight bond of a لأن adjunct. Marked med because I am overriding LAW 4 on two witnesses from a different register. || SITE 195 (probe, lo). The text reads آلاف الكريات الكرات الصغيرة جدا — a gloss with its punctuation stripped, almost certainly الكريات (الكرات) or الكريات، الكرات. Apposition is a cutter in my doctrine three times over (LAW 3 شيئا … شيئا, B5 the comma-set parenthetical @892, G2 the renaming appositive @337). I have zero recorded evidence about parentheses specifically, so I take the single safest bet — one boundary at the opening of the gloss, none at its close — and flag it lo. If the source used parentheses rather than a comma this is a false cut; the 5:1 asymmetry of batch 1 says the probe is worth it. || SITE 216 (probe, lo). وتنقسم كل كرية إلى نصفين نصف أبيض والنصف الآخر أسود. The idiomatic source is إلى نصفين: نصف أبيض والنصف الآخر أسود, and LAW 0's corollary makes a colon a boundary (A4, J1). I deliberately do NOT also cut at 218 before والنصف الآخر أسود, even though C4 (و + new topic NP + nominal predicate) formally licenses it: نصف أبيض والنصف الآخر أسود is a single balanced appositive pair naming the two halves, and cutting it would produce 5/2/4-token fragments — §E/§D density imported into an expository text. One cut, at the colon site, lo. || SITE 232 vs 243 vs 251 (conditionals). Two ف-conditional periods stand back to back: فإذا كانت ... موجبة تكون ... سالبة and فإذا تعرضت ... فإنها تدور .... C1 is explicit that protasis+apodosis is ONE unit, so I cut BEFORE each فإذا (232, 243) and emphatically NOT at 250 before the جواب فإنها. The second period runs 23 tokens with حتى تستقر and بحيث تظهر hanging off it — long, but LAW 4 keeps both limbs inside. Same reasoning kills a cut at 321 before فإنك, which is the apodosis of وأثناء سحبك. || SITE 280 (وهناك). LAW 4's note lists وهناك among forward-attaching adverbials, and LAW 5's @526/@530 case shows وهناك رسالة خاصة welded — but that was inside a quoted letter in §G, where speech welds. Here وهناك عدة أبحاث تجري introduces an existential with a brand-new subject and a whole new research topic. LAW 1 wins. hi. || SITE 297 (وطولها), NOT cut. قطرها عدة سنتيمترات وطولها نحو خمسة وثلاثين سنتيمترا sits inside a بحيث result clause and coordinates two dimensions of one referent — the phrase-level exemption, the same shape as طوله وعرضه. Cutting would strand a 5-token dimension spec as a sentence. || SITE 344 (وربما), NOT cut. وربما بشكل مباشر من خلال قمر صناعي is verbless — an alternative manner-PP sharing تنقل, not a fresh clause. It leaves a 25-token segment, above my band, and K4 does record an emphatic trailing PP getting its own segment — but that was a §K caption. LAW 1's argument test is the primary rule and it says weld. The source mark here is a comma, and in §B commas mostly did not become boundaries (my §B F1 of 96.9–98.8 at ~15 tokens/sentence proves commas were not cutting there). || SITE 362 (probe, lo). والتطور المستقبلي المذهل في مجال صنع الشاشات المرئية الورقية | استخدام الترانزستورات .... A nominal sentence whose مبتدأ runs nine tokens and whose خبر has no هو copula — exactly the configuration Arabic editors punctuate with a colon or dash to stop the reader garden-pathing الورقية استخدام as a continued adjective chain. K3 records the subject-NP/predicate-NP split as a boundary, though only in a caption. §L also names appositive-continuation as my one residual leak in this register. 24 tokens is my second-longest segment. Probe, lo. || SITE 377 (أما), my most confident non-mandatory cut. أما الحبر الإلكتروني ... فإنه يعمل is the canonical Arabic topic-shift period; the correlative ف at 386 is obligatory and must never be cut, which is why 378–405 stays whole at 28 tokens. || SITE 451 (حقا). حقا إن الورق الإلكتروني هو ورق المستقبل الذكي is the closing peroration, 8 tokens, sentence-initial emphatic adverb plus إن. A period precedes it. hi. || Also cut: 138 before وهكذا and 435 before ومن ثم — both discourse-level result connectives heading a full new predication with a new subject, the same shape as C4, and distinct from K5's وهنا (mid-narrative continuation). || FREE BOUNDARIES: 2, 48, 146, 180, 352 (each immediately before an <NL>) and 459 (final).
